name: Elijah
charge: Standing alone against the prophets of Baal, and running before the king in the power of the Lord
summary: Elijah announced the drought to Ahab, received provision at Cherith and Zarephath, and called Israel back to the Lord at Carmel. After Jezebel threatened him, the Lord sustained him in the wilderness and gave him further work, a successor, and assurance that seven thousand had not bowed to Baal. He was later taken up by a whirlwind, and Elisha received his mantle.
offense: Elijah stood before Ahab and declared that there would be neither dew nor rain except according to his word. His authority was expressed in the confession that he stood before the Lord God of Israel (1 Kings 17:1). He did not stand before the king to obtain permission to speak. The king himself was beneath the word he brought. The same word that sent him to announce the drought directed his preservation within it. He went to Cherith, where ravens brought bread and flesh and he drank from the brook. When the brook dried, he went to Zarephath as commanded (1 Kings 17:2-9). Obedience did not keep the brook from drying; it kept him ready to follow the next instruction. The Lord's provision was not confined to one place or one means. When he returned to Ahab, he refused the accusation that he troubled Israel. The trouble arose from forsaking the commandments and following Baalim (1 Kings 18:17-18). At Carmel he called the people to cease halting between two opinions. Their silence could not remain an answer when the question was whom they would serve. He repaired the Lord's altar with twelve stones according to the tribes of Israel, laid the sacrifice in order, and had water poured over it three times. His prayer asked that the people know the Lord was God, that he was the Lord's servant, and that he had done these things at his word (1 Kings 18:30-37). The sign was not sought to establish an independent greatness for the prophet. It was sought to turn the people's hearts back.
